central_topic: Predicting start-averaged expected cover time of simple random walks on small connected graphs (6<=n<=30) with a ridge regression on cheap graph statistics, compared against the generic 2m(n-1) worst-case bound; post-draft citation gaps cover the uncited Aleliunas et al. bound, the Lovász survey, the commute-time/resistance and Matthews-bound literature behind the proposed richer features, and classic ridge regression.
core_methods: Ridge regression of log cover time on log-statistics (n, m, mean degree, max degree, diameter)
Commute-time identity, effective resistance and Matthews-type cover time bounds (proposed richer features, not scored)
comparators: Aleliunas et al. 2m(n-1) cover time bound (headline comparator, currently uncited)
Lovász survey on random walks on graphs (hitting/commute time machinery, currently uncited)

queries.query: Random walks, universal traversal sequences, and the complexity of maze problems
queries.rationale: Related Work and Introduction attribute the 2m(n-1) bound, the paper's headline comparator (bound macro log MAE 1.754), to 'Aleliunas et al.' with no \cite; the bibliography holds only the two Feige papers and Kiwi et al.

queries.query: Lovász Random walks on graphs: a survey
queries.rationale: Related Work 'Worst-case bounds' paragraph names Lovász's survey as the source of hitting-time and commute-time machinery behind such bounds without a citation.

queries.query: Chandra Raghavan Ruzzo Smolensky Tiwari The electrical resistance of a graph captures its commute and cover times
queries.rationale: Discussion ('Feature attribution and ceiling') and Conclusion propose resistance-based features motivated by the commute-time identity; no supporting reference exists in the draft or bibliography.

queries.query: Matthews bounds on covering times of Markov chains via maximum hitting time and harmonic number
queries.rationale: The same Discussion and Conclusion passages cite Matthews-type bounds as the motivation for the richer-feature next step; the Matthews bound is also the basis of the unscored candidate mentioned in the supplementary model-selection note.

queries.query: Hoerl Kennard Ridge regression: biased estimation for nonorthogonal problems
queries.rationale: Related Work 'Statistical prediction with cheap features' and the Method's ridge estimator (needed because three features are collinear) carry no citation; a single classic reference grounds the model class the paper claims no novelty for.

forbidden_query_patterns: broader cover-time literatures for random regular or Erdős–Rényi graphs (deliberately not targeted by the gap artifact)
learned or deep-learning graph-property prediction (not supported by the draft)
re-retrieval of Feige upper/lower bounds or Kiwi et al., which are already in references.bib
queries about run chronology, attempts, or search history
